title.narrative: Enhanced national institutional capacity to establish effective employment services and programmes, thereby streamlining the process of labour market transitions

description.narrative:
Grenada, with a young population and a resilient economy, faces challenges in creating sufficient decent jobs despite its economic growth. High unemployment rates, especially among low-skilled individuals, women, and youth, highlight the need for targeted interventions. The government has adopted policies to address these issues, including an unemployment insurance scheme, but the absence of robust labour market services and programs remains a critical bottleneck.
To address these challenges, the CPO involves conducting robust labour market analyses, establishing an agile public employment services (PES) unit within the Ministry of Legal Affairs, Labour and Consumer Affairs, and capacitating this unit to deliver responsive labour market services and programs. The PES unit will work closely with a wide range of partners, including employers and jobseekers, to facilitate transitions into decent jobs, particularly for youth, women, and low-skilled individuals. The implementation will be guided by relevant ILO conventions and a comprehensive mapping of existing employment policies.
